articles.title: Taliban Reportedly Bars Women's Names From Records in Afghan Province
articles.excerpt: Officials and healthcare workers in Balkh province have reportedly been told to replace women's first names with the generic 'Bibi' in documents, medical records and prescriptions, with activists reporting degrading animal labels in some cases.
articles.image_caption: Afghan women in burqas carry children along a street in Kandahar, in a file photograph. Authorities in Balkh province have reportedly ordered women's first names removed from official documents, medical records and prescriptions.
articles.nri_angle: A world story with no direct reader action; it documents a reported further restriction on Afghan women's legal and medical identity.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Lalah Osmany launches the #WhereIsMyName campaign
Government approves voluntary inclusion of women's names on children's birth certificates
Taliban returns to power in Afghanistan
El País reports the Balkh province order barring women's names from official and medical records

articles.title: Ships Struck Twice in Hormuz as Repeat Attacks Test Tanker Traffic
articles.excerpt: At least six vessels have been hit more than once in two months in the Strait of Hormuz, consultants say. Whether the repeats are deliberate deterrence or the arithmetic of a shrinking target pool is disputed, but traffic through the chokepoint has not stopped.
articles.image_caption: Cargo ships sit at anchor at sunset in a file photograph of Gulf shipping. At least six vessels have been struck more than once in the Strait of Hormuz in October and November, according to security consultancy EOS Risk.
articles.nri_angle: Gulf crude flows through Hormuz supply India and Asia; sustained disruption feeds into fuel and freight prices diaspora readers pay.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Tanker Gem No 2 attacked on October 9 and 10; major oil spill near UAE coast
Tara Gas struck on November 16 and 17; caught fire
Joint Maritime Information Center advisory warns deliberate attacks remain highly likely

articles.title: US Measles Cases Pass 6,000 in 2026 as CDC Counts Nine Deaths
articles.excerpt: The CDC counted 6,039 confirmed cases as of November 24 — more than the whole of 2025 — with 97% of cases tied to outbreaks across 47 jurisdictions.
articles.image_caption: The sign outside the headquarters of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The CDC counted 6,039 confirmed measles cases in the United States in 2026 as of November 24.
articles.nri_angle: With 6,039 confirmed US cases and holiday travel ahead, diaspora families should confirm MMR vaccination for children and travelling relatives.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Supreme Court to Hear Arguments Wednesday on State Bans on AR-15 Rifles
articles.excerpt: Challenges to Connecticut's and Cook County's assault-style weapon bans reach the 6-3 conservative court, in a case that turns on whether America's most popular rifle is in 'common use' — and therefore cannot be banned.
articles.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C., photographed at dusk.
articles.nri_angle: The decision will set the reach of the Second Amendment for every state ban in the country, including in states with large Indian-American populations such as Illinois, New Jersey and California.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Zelenskyy Warns of Major New Russian Strike as Trump Urges Putin to Pull Back
articles.excerpt: Ukraine says Russia is completing preparations for a massive strike on its energy grid. Trump says he pressed Putin in China to end military aggression across Europe, while his envoys describe the peace talks as deadlocked over territory.
articles.image_caption: During a working trip to Kharkiv region, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited the frontline command post of the defenders of Kupyansk and presented state awards. "Unfortunately, we have information about a new mass strike being prepared by the Russians," Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address, according to Al Jazeera.
articles.image_credit: Photo: President Of Ukraine from Україна via Wikimedia Commons (CC0)
articles.nri_angle: The warning concerns Ukraine's power grid heading into winter; there is no direct action for diaspora readers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Israel Kills Hamas Deputy Education Minister in Third Night of Gaza Strikes
articles.excerpt: At least nine Palestinians were killed overnight, medics said, as Israel pressed a campaign of targeted killings and Hamas weighed its response under a ceasefire that has not stopped the violence.
articles.nri_angle: A widening Gaza escalation would test the US-brokered ceasefire plan Washington is pressing both sides to implement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Black Sea Incidents Surge Tenfold, Raising Risk NATO Is Drawn Into War
articles.excerpt: Drones, mines and ship attacks in the Black Sea have risen from fewer than 50 incidents in 2025 to as many as 500 this year, NATO's spokesperson told CBS News, on a sea bordered by three alliance members.
articles.image_caption: Archival satellite photograph: the Black Sea from orbit, taken by NASA in May 2004.
articles.nri_angle: Disruption to Black Sea grain and fuel shipping would feed into global food and fuel prices, including in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Houthis Threaten Jeddah and All Saudi Red Sea Ports as Strikes Escalate
articles.excerpt: The Houthi warning to evacuate Saudi Red Sea ports came hours before the Saudi-led coalition struck Hodeidah, a day after a Houthi drone hit Riyadh's tallest tower and injured at least 11 people.
articles.image_caption: The Jeddah waterfront on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast.
articles.nri_angle: The escalation moves from Riyadh — where two Indians were injured in Tuesday's tower strike — to Saudi Arabia's Red Sea ports, widening the risk map for the Gulf's large Indian workforce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Over 2,300 Indian Sikh Pilgrims Mark Guru Nanak's 557th Birthday in Pakistan
articles.excerpt: More than 5,000 worshippers attended the main ceremony at Gurdwara Janam Asthan in Nankana Sahib on Tuesday, as the Indian jatha's pilgrimage continues to Panja Sahib, Kartarpur and Lahore before the December 1 return.
articles.nri_angle: The annual Nankana Sahib yatra is a central pilgrimage for Sikhs in India and the diaspora; the Kartarpur Corridor's continued closure shapes how devotees can travel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Main ceremony at Gurdwara Janam Asthan

Return to India via Wagah

articles.title: Two Indians Among 11 Injured as Houthis Strike Riyadh Finance District Tower
articles.excerpt: Saudi Civil Defence said a tower in the King Abdullah Financial District was hit in a terrorist attack on Tuesday. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh confirmed two Indian nationals were injured and said assistance is being extended to them and their families.
articles.nri_angle: Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world; the Indian Embassy in Riyadh has confirmed the two injured Indians and is the point of contact for families seeking information.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: First strike on the financial district tower; building damaged, no injuries reported
Second strike injures 11 people, including two Indian nationals

articles.title: Bihar Porter Sold Land to Send Sons to Kota; Both Cracked NEET and JEE
articles.excerpt: Manoj Kumar of Gaya sold one of his family's two plots to fund two years of coaching. Sonu Raj scored 636 in NEET and entered AIIMS CAPFIMS in Delhi; Monu Raj reached BIT Mesra despite months of illness.
articles.nri_angle: A Gaya porter's decision to sell half his land for his sons' Kota coaching — rewarded with medical and engineering admissions — mirrors the education-first sacrifices familiar to diaspora families who funded their own moves abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CrowdStrike to Buy Jay Chaudhry's Zscaler in $43.9 Billion All-Stock Deal
articles.excerpt: The definitive agreement pays Zscaler shareholders 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, an implied $260.41, with Chaudhry staying on to run Zscaler and join the CrowdStrike board.
articles.nri_angle: Zscaler was founded and is led by Indian American chief executive Jay Chaudhry, who will continue to run the business and join CrowdStrike's board if the deal closes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Among 13 Killed as Bus Hits Stopped Truck in Ras Al Khaimah
articles.excerpt: The bus, carrying 41 people, struck a truck that had stopped on Al Watan Road after a mechanical failure. India's consulate in Dubai has contacted bereaved families and opened a 24/7 helpline, 800-46342.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals are among the dead in the UAE's second fatal crash involving Indians in two weeks; the Dubai consulate helpline is the families' first point of contact.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson Issues Proclamation Recognising Diwali; Cook County Follows
articles.excerpt: The mayor's proclamation, dated November 23, honours Diwali's significance for Hindu and Jain communities and acknowledges the Sikh observance of Bandi Chhor Divas; a companion Cook County resolution was adopted on November 19.
articles.image_caption: Downtown Chicago, photographed from above with Lake Michigan behind the skyline. Mayor Brandon Johnson issued a proclamation recognising Diwali dated November 23, 2026, and Cook County adopted a companion resolution.
articles.nri_angle: A major US city and its county have formally recognised the diaspora's biggest festival in the same season its temples are reviewing security after an attempted attack in Aurora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi's December Canada Visit Is Set to Move Ties in a New Direction
articles.excerpt: Jaishankar and Anand call the December 11-12 visit a "building block" as analyst Vina Nadjibulla argues the India-Canada reset must go beyond trade and rebuild trust on the security track too.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Modi will visit Toronto and Ottawa on December 11 and 12 in a trip both governments describe as a building block in rebuilt India-Canada ties.
articles.nri_angle: For Canada's Indian diaspora, the December visit's CEPA and security-dialogue outcomes will shape trade, travel and community confidence after the 2023 rupture.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Congress Seeks Over 100 UP Seats as Seat-Sharing Talks With SP Open in Delhi
articles.excerpt: The two INDIA bloc allies began formal negotiations on Monday for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, with the SP insisting that winnability, not seat counts, should drive the allocation.
articles.image_caption: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, right, speaks at an event in New Delhi in an August 29 file photograph. Gandhi and SP president Akhilesh Yadav held preliminary seat-sharing discussions on November 16, ahead of the formal Congress-SP talks that opened on November 23.
articles.nri_angle: The UP seat-sharing outcome will shape the opposition alliance diaspora voters from Uttar Pradesh follow ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Navdeep Bains Wins Ontario Liberal Leadership on Final Ballot, 50.3 to 49.7
articles.excerpt: The former federal industry minister from Mississauga beat MPP Lee Fairclough by less than a point after a nine-month race, and now has to rebuild a party that holds 14 seats.
articles.image_caption: Navdeep Bains speaks in Toronto during coverage of the Ontario Liberal Party leadership result. Bains won the leadership on the third ballot on November 21, 2026, with 50.3 per cent of the weighted points.
articles.nri_angle: A Sikh former federal minister from Mississauga — home to one of Canada's largest South Asian communities — now leads a major provincial party.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Edmonton's Sneha Joy Wins $5 Million Lotto 6/49 Jackpot
articles.excerpt: Joy matched all six numbers in the October 21 Classic draw with a ticket bought on the Lotto Spot app, and plans to clear her mortgage, travel the world and share with family.
articles.image_caption: Sneha Joy holds a $5,000,000 Lotto Spot cheque dated October 21, 2026, for the Lotto 6/49 draw. The Edmonton winner matched all six numbers in the Classic draw, the Western Canada Lottery Corporation announced.
articles.nri_angle: A Malayali-named Edmonton winner's mortgage-first, family-sharing plan is the kind of diaspora good-news story readers in Canada and Kerala follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Neena Gupta, Who Answered a 70-Year-Old Maths Problem, Named to TIME100 Next India
articles.excerpt: The ISI Kolkata professor found a counterexample to the Zariski Cancellation Problem in 2014. TIME's new India list puts her among its Health and Science Innovators.
articles.image_caption: Mathematician Neena Gupta, a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute in Kolkata, in a photograph published by Mint. Gupta has been named to the TIME100 Next India 2026 list for her work on the Zariski Cancellation Problem.
articles.nri_angle: A Kolkata-educated mathematician recognised on TIME's India list is a reference point for diaspora families weighing research careers and STEM paths for their children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi High Court Orders Fresh Notice in Amrit Wilson OCI Cancellation Case
articles.excerpt: Justice Amit Mahajan held that the 2023 order cancelling the UK-based author's OCI card named no specific 'anti-India activities,' denying her a chance to respond — and set a fixed timetable for the Centre to redo the process.
articles.nri_angle: For OCI cardholders, the ruling sets a procedural floor: before a cancellation can stand, the government must spell out the specific allegations — or at least a redacted gist — so the holder can actually answer them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Wilson granted an OCI card
Centre cancels her OCI registration under Section 7D(e)
Delhi High Court orders a fresh show cause notice within one week

articles.title: Tanker Hit Near Khasab as Hormuz Traffic Stays About 65% Below Pre-War Levels
articles.excerpt: UKMTO reported a fresh projectile strike on an outbound tanker on Saturday, six tanker attacks in a week, and oil flows down to about 10 million barrels a day — with Indian crew among the week's casualties.
articles.image_caption: Khasab, on Oman's Musandam Peninsula at the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.nri_angle: Indian seafarers crew many Gulf tankers and Gulf-based Indian families live beside ports running at a third of pre-war traffic — the strait's closure is a direct diaspora story, not a distant one.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
